CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Fetal tissue (placental material)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRING PHYSICIAN
Dr. [redacted name]
[redacted location] Obstetrics and Gynecology

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing of fetal tissue

TEST PERFORMED
Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH) with QF-PCR

METHODOLOGY
Array CGH analysis was performed using custom design oligonucleotide microarray platform with genome-wide coverage. Data analysis was conducted using the GRCh37/hg19 reference genome assembly. The array platform provides high-resolution detection of copy number variants across all chromosomes with the following capabilities:
- Detection of imbalances >1Mb with high confidence
- Coverage of clinically significant microdeletion/microduplication regions
- Pericentromeric and subtelomeric coverage
- Backbone coverage at approximately 100kb resolution

Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) was performed as an adjunct test specifically to exclude triploidy, which may not be reliably detected by array CGH alone.

RESULTS

ARRAY CGH FINDINGS:
Result: arr(1-22)x2,(XY)x1
Interpretation: Normal male chromosome complement

No copy number imbalances detected in clinically significant regions
No imbalances >1Mb identified throughout the genome
All autosomes (chromosomes 1-22): Normal copy number (x2)
Sex chromosomes: XY male pattern

QF-PCR RESULTS:
Triploidy excluded
Normal diallelic patterns observed for all markers tested

INTERPRETATION
The array CGH analysis demonstrates a normal male chromosome complement without evidence of clinically significant chromosomal imbalances. The resolution of this test excludes deletions and duplications greater than 1Mb in size. QF-PCR analysis has excluded triploidy.

These results are consistent with a chromosomally normal male fetus.

TECHNICAL LIMITATIONS
1. Array CGH cannot detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements (translocations, inversions)
2. Low-level mosaicism (<20-30%) may not be detected
3. Copy number variants smaller than the resolution of the array platform may not be detected
4. Uniparental disomy cannot be detected by this methodology
5. Point mutations and small insertions/deletions are not detected

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is required based on these results.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Cytogenetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director

Electronically signed: [redacted date]
